subject: Clarify PHI egress controls and BAA scope for Pharmaco / Helios pilot
messages:
From: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@pharmaco.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@heliospharma.com>, security@heliospharma.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PHI handling for pilot — quick clarifying questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Helios is keen to run a short pilot ingesting provider-supplied patient records for medication reconciliation. Before we proceed we'd like to confirm a couple of things for our security and legal teams: 

- Where does PHI live during processing (hosted vs dedicated vs private)?
- Can you restrict any egress to our VPC / approved S3 buckets only?
- Is Redwood able to sign a BAA limited to the pilot scope (~6 weeks)?

I attached our baseline HIPAA questionnaire to this thread (Pharmaco_HIPAA_Qs.pdf). Can you confirm the high-level controls and any limitations we should be aware of?

Best,
Alex
Director, Partnerships
Pharmaco Therapeutics

[Attachment: Pharmaco_HIPAA_Qs.pdf (pdf)]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@pharmaco.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@heliospharma.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PHI handling for pilot — quick clarifying questions

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front and I copied the engineering leads for specifics: 

1) Processing location: we support three deployment modes. For pilot purposes we recommend Redwood Dedicated (isolated GPU pool) or Redwood Private (VPC) so PHI never traverses multi-tenant host paths. Hosted API can be used only with a strict contractual exception and additional controls.

2) Egress restrictions: yes — for Dedicated and Private we can lock outbound egress to a customer-controlled VPC endpoint or to allowlisted S3 buckets. We'll need the destination bucket ARNs and egress IP ranges to configure firewall rules.

3) BAA: Redwood signs BAAs for customers processing PHI. We can offer a timeboxed BAA for the pilot; legal prefers a clear scope and termination/hand-off clauses. I've attached our initial draft BAA for your review (Redwood_Draft_BAA_v1.docx).

Next steps: Monica will outline the specific network controls and Dev will confirm retention and encryption behavior. Can you confirm the pilot ingest volume and target retention window?

Thanks,
Naomi
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Redwood_Draft_BAA_v1.docx (docx)]

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@pharmaco.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 12:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PHI handling for pilot — network/evidence details

Alex — a few technical clarifications from the infra side: 

- Deployment recommendation: Redwood Private (VPC) so we can place the inference nodes in your subnet and enforce egress via your NAT / egress gateway. If you prefer we can also provide Dedicated with allowlisted egress to your S3 buckets.
- Egress locking: we support explicit egress policy configurations at the node pool level. We'll need: destination S3 bucket ARNs, destination IP ranges (if you want IP allowlist as well), and whether you require TLS mutual auth for S3 endpoints.
- Logging / audit: we can provide per-request audit logs and signed S3 access logs. For HIPAA evidence you may ask for sample logs — we can provide time-limited access links.

Also attaching a simple network diagram showing the proposed flow and where PHI is resident during processing (egress-diagram.png).

Thanks — Monica
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: egress-diagram.png (png)]

From: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@pharmaco.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@heliospharma.com>, security@heliospharma.com
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PHI handling for pilot — network/evidence details

Thanks Naomi / Monica — helpful. A couple of follow-ups from Legal & Security: 

- Pilot scope: ~100k patient records, retention for pilot 30 days after ingestion (we'll delete), then data handed back to Helios.
- We need explicit confirmation that no PHI will be replicated outside the configured buckets / VPC for any backups, telemetry, or analytics.
- Please indicate whether key material for encryption is customer-managed (KMS/HSM) or Redwood-managed for the pilot.

Can you mark the BAA draft with the pilot timeframe and the network constraints so we can circulate internally?

Alex

[Forwarded attachment: Pharmaco_HIPAA_Qs.pdf]

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@pharmaco.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 09:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PHI handling for pilot — technical confirmation

Hi all — technical confirmations below: 

- No replication outside configured storage or VPC: Confirmed for Redwood Private and Dedicated. Our control plane (for Private) can be run in a customer-managed control plane; logs that contain PHI are only written to the customer S3 bucket if you opt in. By default we redact PHI from operational telemetry.
- Backups: we do not take system backups of customer buckets. Any backups are customer-managed. For Dedicated, snapshots are possible but can be disabled for pilot.
- Encryption keys: we support customer-managed KMS keys for S3 and for disk encryption. For the pilot we recommend customer-managed keys (we provide simple instructions to grant the Redwood service principal encrypt/decrypt access scoped to the pilot buckets).
- Retention/deletion: we support lifecycle rules and an API-driven purge. We will provide an automated deletion run after 30 days and can provide an attestable deletion report (hash + timestamp).

I'll add a short appendix to the BAA draft describing these behaviors.

—Dev
Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

[No attachments]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@pharmaco.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PHI handling for pilot — summary & next steps

Alex / Liam — thanks for the prompt answers and the pilot parameters. Summary & next steps: 

1) Scope: pilot = 100k records, retention 30 days, deletion and attestable report after retention window.
2) Deployment: Redwood Private (preferred) or Dedicated with egress allowlist to Helios S3.
3) Controls: customer-managed KMS recommended; per-request audit logs available; operational telemetry redacted by default.
4) BAA: Naomi to circulate timeboxed BAA v1 with explicit pilot scope and termination clauses. Monica/Dev to add appendix on egress, key mgmt, backups, and attestable deletion.

Action items: 
- Naomi: send updated BAA by EOD Fri (2027-03-26).
- Alex: share destination bucket ARNs and any IP ranges you want allowlisted.
- Dev/Monica: prepare sample audit log extract and network configuration summary.

If that all looks right we'll prepare a short runbook and schedule a technical onboarding session.

Best,
Naomi
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Redwood_Draft_BAA_v1.docx (docx) — updated v1.1 to follow]
